0.content:
Aberrant Chimeric Monster (also: Aberrant Chimeric Monsters, Aberrant Chimeras, chimeric beasts, man-made monsters of Snezhnaya, Koshchei's chimeras): Aberrant Chimeric Monsters are the hybrid beasts of Snezhnaya, products of the bio-alchemy that flourished before it was forbidden. In the reign of the Belyi Tsar alchemists, above all Koshchei, freely combined living things into new animals. Most were consumed in the war against the Onslaught of Dark Beasts, and the handful that survive are rare, dangerous exceptions. They include armoured beasts, burrowing predators, winged elephants, horned bears, the two-headed Chimeric Winged Lion and the Immortal Construct.

Nature: Man-made monsters from Snezhnayan bio-alchemy, combining the traits of different animals. In-game text describes them as pieces of life, scattered like puzzle parts, put together as the researchers pleased.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 only scattered survivors remain across Snezhnaya, wild and hostile. Zver is dead.

1.content:
Abyss Herald (also: Abyss Heralds, Wicked Torrents, Frost Fall, Presager of the Abyss, Fortune Lector): Abyss Heralds are elite melee fighters of the Abyss Order who command intense Abyssal power through blades. They come in two kinds: Wicked Torrents (Hydro) and Frost Fall (Cryo). The Archive calls them silent vanguards and envoys of the Abyss, counterparts to the singing, ranged Abyss Lectors. Most are anonymous. Klingsor, a one-time Sumeru Skeptic who embraced the Abyss, is the best-known named Herald.

Nature: A Herald is a person-sized, humanoid creature of the Abyss, armed with a sword of water or ice. Archive text for Wicked Torrents calls the type silent figures at the Abyss's vanguard whose tidal blades "engulf everything in an instant"; the Frost Fall entry says that just as saints spread the gospel, there are envoys to correct twisted strains and remove dissonance, and that their dark frost is said to freeze even the soul.

Abilities and limits: Fast, aggressive melee attackers, with some ranged attacks. In the Hydro form the blades throw torrents of water; in the Cryo form, bursts of ice. At low health a Herald raises a tough elemental shield and falls the moment that shield breaks.

Relations: Heralds serve the Abyss Order, and so, indirectly, its leader, the Traveler's Sibling. Their natural enemies are the Traveler, Dainsleif, and the guardians of the lands they attack.

2.content:
Abyss Lector (also: Abyss Lectors, Fathomless Flames, Violet Lightning, Abyss Chanter): Abyss Lectors are the ranged elites of the Abyss Order, spellcasters who chant over books and verses and fight with catalysts. They are the counterpart of the melee Abyss Heralds. There are two kinds: Violet Lightning (Electro, debuted 1.5) and Fathomless Flames (Pyro, added 2.4). The best-known individual is Enjou, a Pyro Lector who posed as a human clerk in Enkanomiya and kept turning up afterwards, as Sanka and under other names, in Natlan.

Nature: Archive text calls the Fathomless Flames Lector a wielder of abyssal fire who pursues the meaning behind texts and scriptures, and says that reading "the word of grace" grants them great power. Violet Lightning Lectors are called the evangelists and scholars of the Abyss, who sing the praises of darkness and strike the hearts of unbelievers with violent violet lightning.

Abilities and limits: Ranged elemental attacks with a catalyst, shielding themselves when wounded.

Relations: Lectors serve the Abyss Order and its leader, the Traveler's Sibling. They are opposed by the Traveler, Dainsleif, and the people whose lands they invade.

3.content:
Abyss Mage (also: Abyss Mages, Pyro Abyss Mage, Hydro Abyss Mage, Cryo Abyss Mage, Electro Abyss Mage, Pyrochanter, Hydrochanter, Cryochanter): Abyss Mages are the Abyss Order's everyday spellcasters: hooded, masked creatures who command one of four elements (Pyro, Hydro, Cryo, Electro) and shield themselves behind a barrier of that element. Adventurers say they sit at the lowest rung of the Order's ranks. They are usually found near hilichurls, whom they can talk to and manipulate, or with other mages. They are far weaker than Abyss Heralds and Lectors, but still dangerous.

Nature: Archive text calls them "Abyss creatures" that can command the elements to a limited extent. The Adventurer Handbook says that, for unknown reasons, they can speak with hilichurls and so bend their minds easily, and that the language they chant is long forgotten and the source of their magic.

Abilities and limits: Mages fire elemental bolts and cast area spells from range. Their key defence is an elemental shield, and breaking it leaves the mage stunned and exposed.

Relations: Mages serve the Abyss Order and, through it, the Order's leader, the Traveler's Sibling. They command hilichurls; Dainsleif says many hilichurls are cursed Khaenri'ahns whom the Abyss Order conscripts.

4.content:
Adeptus (also: Adepti, Mighty and Illuminated Adepti, Mighty and Illuminated Adeptus, adeptal beings): The adepti (singular adeptus) are Liyue's immortal guardians. Most are illuminated beasts: ancient cranes, deer, qilin and similar creatures that speak, live for millennia and wield elemental power. A few gods are also counted among them. Most signed a contract with Rex Lapis (Morax), the "Prime of Adepti", to protect Liyue from demons and evil gods, and they fought beside him in the Archon War. Afterwards most withdrew to the mountains of Jueyun Karst. Well-known adepti include Cloud Retainer, Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper, Madame Ping, Xiao and the half-qilin Ganyu.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the adepti still guard Liyue, mostly from seclusion. Rex Lapis lives on as Zhongli. Cloud Retainer (as Xianyun) and Madame Ping live in Liyue Harbor, and Xiao keeps watch from Wangshu Inn.

5.content:
Aeonblight Drake (also: Perpetual Motion GL-Faf, Perpetual Motion Dragon, Aeonblight Drake (Heavy Assault Pack)): The Aeonblight Drake is a huge dragon-shaped combat machine, one of the Ruin Machines, found in Sumeru in the Ardravi Valley area of Devantaka Mountain. Its boss title is Perpetual Motion GL-Faf. It is a normal boss that fights on the ground and in the air, and it can take on and use the element that has harmed it most.

Nature: A tireless machine built in the shape of a dragon, with thrusters, a tail, a head it can strike with, and an element-storing core in its neck.

key: Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network
Tomb Guard of the Desert King
6.comment: Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network
6.content:
Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network (also: Tomb Guard of the Desert King, Matrix of Overseer Network, ASIMON, Field Annihilation Array, Anoushbord): The Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network is a large Primal Construct, an automaton left by the ancient civilisation of King Deshret. It is a normal boss found at the Dune of Elusion in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru, with the boss title Tomb Guard of the Desert King. It fights with lasers and by turning invisible behind deployed parts.

Nature: A perpetual-motion machine from an ancient desert civilisation, working as a governing node over lesser constructs.

key: Visitor from the Far Side of the Sea of Stars
7.content:
All-Devouring Narwhal (also: Visitor from the Far Side of the Sea of Stars, the All-Devouring Narwhal): The All-Devouring Narwhal is a colossal whale-like creature from the sea of stars, outside Teyvat's sky. It is the pet of Surtalogi the Foul, Skirk's master. It fed on the Primordial Sea beneath Fontaine, which made the sea level rise, and its rampage set off the flood the Prophecy of Fontaine foretold. Neuvillette and the Traveler defeated it in the Primordial Sea, and Skirk shrank it to an orb and took it away.

Nature: A vast, mysterious creature "from another world". Neuvillette describes it as a monster that crossed the stars weeping. It is not a native of Teyvat and belongs to no known species. It devours, and it craves energy and living things.

Abilities and limits: It swims through solid ground as if it were water, rising to leap or dive at its target. It conjures falling crystals and beams of light, and it can swallow a fighter whole.

Relations: Surtalogi owns it. Skirk, his disciple, defeated and shrank it when it threatened her student. Tartaglia has an old tie with it, and he built the whale shape into his own fighting style after meeting it.

8.content:
Aranara (also: Aranaras, forest spirits of Sumeru): The Aranara are small, plantlike forest spirits of Sumeru, living mainly in Vanarana, a village hidden inside a dream in Dharma Forest. The Dendro Archon Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, whom they called Queen Aranyani, made them to guard the forest and its creatures. They are friendly, curious and easily frightened, shy of adults, close to children, and they treasure memories and songs.

Nature: Aranara come in many shapes, colours and hats (a mushroom cap, a pair of leaves) and always seem to smile. Many have a leaf on top of the head that works as a small propeller and lets them fly. They do not need to sleep or eat, are very afraid of fire and salt, and can be revitalised with Dendro energy.

Abilities and limits: Each Aranara has its own Ararakalari, powers drawn from its memories and channelled through the plants of the forest. They can fight, restrain or weaken enemies, shield against the Withering, teleport over great distances in an instant and seal off areas.

Society: The Aranara live in Vanarana, a hidden village. Their elder Araja and the lively Arana are two of the main figures; most Aranara have names beginning "Ara-".

9.content: Augury Bird (also: Augury Birds, Augury Bird fae): Augury Birds are a rare, short-lived kind of Snowland Fae from Snezhnaya. They grow a pair of small wings on their heads, which can pass for ordinary hair under a hat, and are born able to see "crossroads in the flow of fate" for themselves alone. Very few are alive. The two known ones are the sisters Celaeno and Linnea; Linnea was raised as a human child in Nod-Krai.

10.content:
Automatons (also: Automaton, Automatons family, Mechanical enemies, Primal Constructs, Secret Source Automatons, Domain Keepers): "Automatons" is the game's name for mechanical enemies. They are not one race or one invention: the family groups machines built by different, often long-dead makers. The biggest group is the Ruin Machines of Khaenri'ah (which have their own entry). The rest are Primal Constructs from King Deshret's desert, Clockwork Meka built in Fontaine, Secret Source Automatons found in Natlan and on the Frost Moon, and the Domain Keepers of the Temple of Space. Most fight with physical force and have no will of their own.

Nature: Machines, not living creatures. Most still active are leftovers of lost civilisations with no master left; dormant ones wake when someone comes near.

Groups: - Ruin Machines (1.0): Khaenri'ah's, own entry.
- Primal Constructs (3.1): Deshret's desert guardians.
- Clockwork Meka (4.0): Fontaine's, charged with Arkhe.
- Secret Source Automatons (5.0): Natlan's ancient machines, plus a Frost Moon variant (6.7).
- Domain Keepers (6.5): Temple of Space guardians.

Abilities and limits: Mostly Physical damage and a weak point that stuns them when hit; several groups have a trick such as invisibility or retaliation.

11.content:
Avatar of Lava (also: Avatars of Lava, Eroding Avatar of Lava, Fluid Avatar of Lava, Lava Dragon Statue, Seeing Eyes): Avatars of Lava are elite creatures of Natlan with a core of lava. They must keep absorbing heat to stay active, and are often found dormant until the Traveler uses Elemental Sight. Archive text treats them as hollow leftovers of very old attempts to make life from fire and phlogiston, with no more will than a stone. Two ordinary types exist (Eroding and Fluid) and one boss form, the Lava Dragon Statue.

Nature: A strange monster that needs to absorb thermal energy continually or it goes inert. Its heart is a core of molten rock and the body is built from stone around it.

Abilities and limits: They fight in melee and with eruptions of heat. Eroding types are of the Geo kind; Fluid types are Pyro.

12.content:
Bake-Danuki (also: tanuki, tanuki youkai, raccoon dog youkai): Bake-danuki, also just called tanuki, are youkai of Inazuma that look like small plump raccoon dogs, often with a leaf on the head and a bag around the neck. They can transform into objects and even people, and love pranking humans. Their leader is Ioroi, the Hidden Protector of the Grove, sealed inside a large statue in Chinju Forest.

Nature: Youkai tricksters. They shapeshift into objects and people, and the Archive stresses they mean no harm.

Abilities and limits: Transformation into objects and humans, and illusions. They are not fighters.

Society: Loose communities under one leader, Ioroi, who lives in Chinju Forest on Narukami Island.

Relations: Rivals and sometime friends of the kitsune. They tangle with the Shogunate's officers when pranks go too far.

13.content:
Bathysmal Vishap (also: Bathysmal Vishaps, Dragonheirs of the Depths, Dragonheir of the Depths, Hydro Vishaps, Coral Defenders, Bathysmal Vishap Herd, Rimebiter Bathysmal Vishap, Bolteater Bathysmal Vishap): Bathysmal Vishaps, called the Dragonheirs of the Depths by the people of Enkanomiya, are a race of vishaps that live in the deep sea. They are aggressive toward humans, refuse man-made light, and adapt so quickly that individuals can carry Hydro, Cryo or Electro. They terrorised Enkanomiya (Byakuyakoku) for thousands of years until the Watatsumi Omikami suppressed them under the sea with jade coral. In recent years a few have appeared in Fontaine.

Nature: Vishaps of the Light Realm, living in the deep sea and in the caverns of Enkanomiya. The Adventurer Handbook calls them a mighty race that hates light not from weak eyesight, but because the sunlight and the surface world were taken from them, so they refuse man-made light.

Abilities and limits: Individuals can carry Hydro, Cryo or Electro, and some wield more than one element. A signature attack, Cleansing Shower, drains Energy from its target, and a target without enough Energy loses HP instead.

14.content:
Breacher Primus (also: Breacher Primuses, Overgrown Breacher Primus, Shatterstone Breacher Primus, Elynas' cells): Breacher Primuses are elite creatures of Fontaine, aligned with the Abyss and found mostly in and around the body of Elynas. The Archive calls them a strange life form with no known kin among Teyvat's creatures. According to Elynas himself they are his cells, made after his death, and they work like a body's defenders, driving harmful things away from him and his children.

Nature: Alien, Abyss-aligned lifeforms that behave like the defensive cells of a giant body. They are tied to Elynas, the great beast whom the Melusines call "Father".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 they remain as hostile creatures in and around Elynas in Fontaine's depths. No later canon changes their nature.

15.content:
Cicin (also: Cicins, Electro Cicin, Hydro Cicin, Cryo Cicin, Fatui Cicin Mage, Fatui Cicin Mages, Cicin Mage): Cicins are small, bat-like creatures that can slightly manipulate an element (Electro, Hydro or Cryo). Individually weak, they fly nimbly, fire elemental bolts, and avoid predators by their agility. Fatui Cicin Mages command them in battle.

Nature: Cicins are small flying creatures tied to one element each. Canon documents Electro, Hydro and Cryo varieties. They are fragile but quick.

Abilities and limits: Cicins fly and shoot small bolts of their element at people. They are fragile; their danger is in agility and numbers.

Relations: The Fatui use Cicins: Fatui Cicin Mages summon and command them, using their fondness for Mist Grass.

16.content:
Clockwork Meka (also: Clockwork Mek, Mek, Meks, Meka, Fontaine meka, Fontainian automatons): Clockwork Meka (singular Mek) are Fontaine's machines: clockwork automatons that were built as laborers and surveyors and later modified for combat. They are powered by Arkhe, the Pneuma and Ousia energies native to Fontaine, which lets them deal elemental damage. Most are not truly intelligent. They are used by the Maison Gardiennage, sold to private citizens, and favored by thieves and brigands.

Nature: Meka are powered by Arkhe. A mek is either Pneuma-aligned (its clockwork glows bright white) or Ousia-aligned (dark blue) and uses different attacks depending on which. Hit it with the opposite Arkhe and it temporarily loses its energy: it is reduced to physical attacks, or cannot attack at all. Some models deal the same damage type whichever way they are aligned.

17.content:
Consecrated Beast (also: Consecrated Beasts, Consecrated Fanged Beast, Consecrated Flying Serpent, Consecrated Horned Crocodile, Consecrated Red Vulture, Consecrated Scorpion, Phagocytic Form): Consecrated Beasts are wild animals that fed on the remains of gods or similarly powerful beings and were warped by them. They grew huge and strong, sprouted bone-like growths they cannot shed, and now fight with elemental attacks. They are elite enemies, found mostly in Sumeru and rarely in Inazuma and Fontaine. Five kinds are known: fanged beast (Dendro), flying serpent (Anemo), horned crocodile (Hydro), red vulture (Pyro) and scorpion (Electro).

Nature: Ordinary animals, not a separate species: a predator, a reptile, a scavenger bird or an arthropod that ate the corpse of a far greater being and lived. They could not fully digest it, so the remains fused with their bodies into a bony shell.

18.content:
Domain Keeper (also: Domain Keepers, Segment-Domain Keeper, Segment-Domain Keepers, Pillar Hall guardian): Domain Keepers are elite enemies of the automaton family, shadow constructs that guard the Temple of Space, the Pillar Hall floating above Windrest Peak in Mondstadt. They arrived with the Temple of Space in Version 6.5 (Luna VI). They fight in Geo with materialised swords and can briefly take on the element they are struck with.

Nature: In the Archive they are shadow constructs "born of a flow" from the primordial being, the Heavenly Principles, and they stand guard over the Pillar Hall of the heavens. They are not living animals or angels.

Abilities and limits: Fights with Geo: hand and wing strikes, plus a sword that appears in its hand for spinning slashes, lunges and thrown blades. Its signature Deluded Eye state monitors Pyro, Hydro, Electro and Cryo hits; after enough hits of one element it transforms into that element with an immutable aura and strong resistance, then ends in a heavy ground slam.

19.content:
Domovoy (also: Domovoi, household fae, Grand Duke of the Domovoy): The Domovoy, "household fae", are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae. They are short, very long-lived people native to Snezhnaya. They were traditionally ruled by a Grand Duke of the Domovoy. The Fifth Harbinger Pulcinella (Mirko Radovidovich Veleshek) is a Domovoy, as were the late Grand Duke Alvis and Izmaylov, the president of the Royal Energy Commission.

Nature: Domovoy are known for their small stature. They count among the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, alongside Vila, Leshy, Volkodlak, Snegovik and Jack Frost. Their name is the Russian word for a house spirit.

20.content:
Dragon (also: Dragons, dragonkind, dragon race, dragons of Teyvat): Dragons are enormous elemental beings of the Light Realm and the original masters of Teyvat. The old world was ruled by the Dragon King Nibelung and the Seven Sovereigns, one elemental dragon per element, until the Heavenly Principles arrived, defeated them, took part of their Authorities and remade the world for humanity. Today most dragonkind survives as vishaps, Natlan's saurians and a few great individuals such as Dvalin (Anemo), Azhdaha (Geo), Apep (Dendro) and Neuvillette (Hydro).

Nature: Dragons are born from the elements and live far longer than mortals or even gods. They usually grow stronger with age, and their size tracks their strength: Azhdaha at full power was as large as a mountain range. Their bodies reflect their element, like Azhdaha's stony hide or Dvalin's sleek wind-dragon shape.

History: Long ago the Heavenly Principles came to Teyvat, defeated the Seven Sovereigns with the help of the Four Shades and remade the world for humanity. Dragons who refused to submit, such as the Bathysmal Vishaps, fled into the deep sea.

Abilities and limits: A great dragon commands its element on a national scale and can rival an Archon: Azhdaha, Dvalin and Durin are all described in such terms. Lesser dragons can be killed by strong Vision or Delusion users.

Relations: Most dragons and the gods have been enemies since the Heavenly Principles' conquest, though exceptions exist: Dvalin is Mondstadt's protector, and Azhdaha was once Morax's friend.

Individuals: - Nibelung: the Dragon King, killed by the Heavenly Principles (own entry).
- Living Sovereigns: Dvalin (Anemo), Azhdaha (Geo, sealed), Apep (Dendro), Neuvillette (Hydro, in human form).

21.content:
Elemental Lifeforms (also: Elemental Lifeform, elemental life form, elemental life forms, elemental lifeform): Elemental Lifeforms are creatures made of pure, condensed elemental energy rather than flesh and blood. Each is bound to one element and is immune to it. The family covers the humble slimes, the floating specters, the cube-shelled hypostases (the purest of them), the Tainted Hydro Phantasms of Fontaine, and the Frostnight Scions of Nod-Krai. Canon treats them as dangerous phenomena of living element, not as people.

Nature: Elemental Lifeforms are enemies made purely of one element, to which they are immune. Some apply their own element to themselves, so reactions with that element can still occur on them. Power and size track how much elemental energy went into them.

Abilities and limits: Each lifeform fights with its own element and shrugs off that element. Slimes bump, leap and slam; specters float and explode; hypostases hide in shells and expose a core only when they attack; Phantasms and Scions grow stronger when enraged.

Types: Slimes (small and large, all seven elements; the Prism Slime is a rare special case), specters, hypostases, Tainted Hydro Phantasms, Frostnight Scions.

Relations: Hilichurls throw and ride slimes and use them for shields and weapon infusions. Scholars, cooks and builders find uses for them. Fontaine's Oceanids were replaced by Phantasms.

key: Searing Tide Pulsing Beneath the Mountains
Lone Suzerain of Land and Sea
22.content:
Emperor of Fire and Iron (also: Searing Tide Pulsing Beneath the Mountains, Lone Suzerain of Land and Sea, Armored Crablord, Tyrant of Fire and Iron): The Emperor of Fire and Iron is a colossal Armored Crab that lives in a cavern beneath a lake in Fontaine's Belleau Region. It is an ancient ruler of the Fontemer Aberrants, the strange sea creatures of Fontaine, and wears twin horns that burn with Pyro. It does not hunt travellers; it is an enormous, armoured creature that fights when disturbed. Sailors tell tales about it.

Nature: An Armored Crab (the small shell-borrowing crabs found across Fontaine) that grew far beyond its kin. The Adventurer Handbook calls it an ancient ruler of the Fontemer Aberrants, said to have witnessed Fontaine's seas before the first diluvian period. The tutorial calls it an Armored Crablord that has outlived and outgrown almost every other aberrant.

Abilities and limits: Heavy claw strikes, charges and leaping slams (Physical), and Pyro attacks from the horns: volleys of fireballs that scorch the ground, trails of explosions and a large explosion at the arena centre. While its horns are intact it uses its strongest attacks.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and unchanged as of 7.1: it remains in its cavern as a repeatable boss. I found no mention of it in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content.

key: Fae with Crystals Growing on the Skin
23.content:
Fae of Crystalline Flesh (also: Fae with Crystals Growing on the Skin, hostile Snowland Fae, crystal-skinned fae): "Fae of Crystalline Flesh" is the game's label for the Snowland Fae that fight the Traveler in Snezhnaya. The group covers Snegovik (the ice-mage Glaciomancers, the ice-knight Glacial Wardens and the boss Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow), winged Vila (Halberd-Knight and Soarer Knight), the wolf-like Volkodlak brutes and the tree-like Wildwood Leshies. The Handbook says the crystals on their bodies formed from a surge of energy as they were being crafted into living beings.

Nature: Hostile members of the Snowland Fae, artificial peoples made long ago in Hyperborea and later gathered under the Belyi Tsar. Crystalline growths mark their bodies.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 these fae wander Snezhnaya, and the Guardian Blade (new in 7.1) has left her clan's manor.

24.content: Fisher of Hidden Depths (also: Fishers of Hidden Depths, Hidden Depths Fisher, Deepdark Fisher): Fishers of Hidden Depths are Electro-aligned elite creatures of the Abyss family, first seen in Version 6.3 in the northern reaches of Nod-Krai. They are described as Abyssal creatures that slip through rifts from beyond this world. They come in groups, and their linked Deepdark Shields make a swarm hard to break unless the shield is shattered.

25.content:
Fontemer Aberrant (also: Fontemer Aberrants, Fontemer Aberrant Material, Fontaine sea creatures): Fontemer Aberrants are Fontaine's native aquatic beasts: crabs, octopuses, jellyfish, seahorses, stingrays, sea hares and a whale-like mammal called the Blubberbeast. They live in the waters of Fontaine and along its shores, and they are not recorded anywhere else in Teyvat. Most fight by firing Hydro projectiles or pouncing. They are animals, not a kingdom: the Adventurer Handbook insists they have no courts, words or aristocracy.

Nature: Fontemer Aberrants are ordinary animals as canon describes them, not spirits or people. Most hunt for food and are unaggressive otherwise. Even the largest remain simple creatures that grew powerful by surviving.

Abilities and limits: Hydro projectiles and jets are the common attack: bubbles, water guns, water blades. Crabs and some adults are tougher and hit harder. Giants carry an elemental ward that must be broken before they can be hurt properly.

Society: There is no society. The Handbook calls Fontemer Aberrants simple aquatic animals with no courts, kingdoms or words, and says tales to the contrary are the romantic imagination of people unwilling to accept a bland world.

Relations: People in Fontaine regard them as wildlife to avoid or admire. They are also associated with Fontaine's local waters and, in speculation only, with the Primordial Sea.

Individuals: The two famous individuals are the Emperor of Fire and Iron, a giant Armored Crab, and the Millennial Pearl Seahorse, a violet-lit ancient seahorse. Both live in caverns.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the species is unchanged. Nothing found shows a new Fontemer Aberrant in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 or any appearance outside Fontaine.

26.content: Frostnight Scion (also: Frostnight Scions, Icy Crystal Frostnight Scion, Blazing Brilliance Frostnight Scion, Surging Currents Frostnight Scion, Tangled Vines Frostnight Scion, Gleaming Charge Frostnight Scion, Gilded Sunshard Frostnight Scion, Veiled Cloudchaser Frostnight Scion): Frostnight Scions are elegant, antlered and winged elemental lifeforms found in Nod-Krai, introduced in Version 6.0 (four kinds; three more arrived in 6.3). Their Handbook text says long exposure to high concentrations of elemental energy gave them their present forms. Each kind carries one element (Cryo, Pyro, Hydro, Dendro, Electro, Geo or Anemo), is immune to it, and periodically slips into a stronger Gloomveiled state. Far-northern prayers say they were born from the Frost Moon's blessings.

27.content:
Fungus (also: Fungi, Fungal beasts, Floating Anemo Fungus, Floating Dendro Fungus, Floating Hydro Fungus, Stretchy Anemo Fungus, Stretchy Electro Fungus, Stretchy Geo Fungus): Fungi are mushroom creatures found mainly in Sumeru and, in a few spots, in Liyue. The Adventurer Handbook calls a fungus "the congregation of overgrown and over-evolved spores." Most people treat them as monsters, though some are being tamed. They attack with every element, and Pyro or Electro changes how a fungus behaves.

Nature: A fungus is a spore-born creature that has grown far beyond an ordinary mushroom. It keeps one element, so a given fungus may be Anemo, Cryo, Dendro, Electro, Geo, Hydro or Pyro. Most are animal-like enough to float, stretch, spin or walk.

Habitat: Fungi are common enemies across Sumeru. The Jadeplume Terrorshroom entry notes that fungi grow wherever it is damp and fertile. They do not appear in the Natlan overworld.

Abilities and limits: Each fungus fights with its own element: spore bursts, spinning, stretching strikes or flying charges. Pyro scorches them and Electro activates them, which changes their pace and damage.

Relations: People and fungi are mostly enemies, but there are exceptions. Most people consider fungi monsters, Sumeru scholars from Amurta take an interest in them, and some people raise them.

Individuals: The Jadeplume Terrorshroom, the lord of fungal beasts in Sumeru. Bifrons, the Sage-Lord of Fungi in the Natlan questline. Xamaran, a giant glowing mushroom in the Chasm that can speak.

28.content:
Geovishap (also: Geovishaps, Geo Vishap, Geo Vishaps, Rock-Hard Geo Beast): Geovishaps are large, armoured vishaps native to Liyue's mountains. They are Geo-attuned elite beasts that roll into a ball, slam, and send spikes along the ground. Adults can also soak up Cryo, Pyro, Electro or Hydro from their surroundings and fight with it. They are the grown form of Geovishap Hatchlings and the lesser kin of the great Primo Geovishap.

Nature: Geovishaps are vishaps, dragon-like elemental creatures of the Light Realm, in their Geo line. They are heavily armoured and aggressive towards people. The name is Geo plus "vishap", an Armenian word for dragon.

Habitat: Liyue's rocky country, often in caves and burrows. Known haunts include Tianqiu Valley in Minlin, the Chasm and the highlands of Chenyu Vale.

Abilities and limits: Geovishaps roll into a ball and charge, jump and land with a slam, slash and punch with their claws, and drag out lines of spikes from the ground. Their signature trick is Elemental Conversion: partway through a fight an adult absorbs Cryo, Pyro, Electro or Hydro and hits harder with it.

Relations: Hatchlings are their young. Primo Geovishaps are the larger form. Azhdaha, Geo Dragon Sovereign, is an ancient ancestor of the species. People in Liyue treat them as dangerous beasts.

29.content:
Ghost (also: Ghosts, Spirits, Lingering souls, Shades of Tokoyo, Sinshades): Ghosts, also called spirits, are spectral figures found in many parts of Teyvat. Per the wiki, they are the souls of the dead that linger rather than being reincarnated, though some are better described as memories projected by the Ley Lines. Most keep a human appearance. They are not a single species: each region has its own sort, from Wuwang Hill in Liyue to Enkanomiya, Tsurumi Island, Natlan and Nod-Krai.

Nature: The wiki profile calls ghosts souls that remain in the world and do not get reincarnated for unknown reasons. The ghosts of Wuwang Hill and Tsurumi Island appear instead to be memory recreations made by the Ley Lines.

30.content:
Gosoythoth (also: Reaper of the Abyss, heart of the Abyss, Gosoythoth, Reaper of the Abyss): Gosoythoth, titled the Reaper of the Abyss, was a powerful sapient entity that Natlan's defenders called the heart of the Abyss. When the Abyss put out the Sacred Flame, it manifested over the Stadium of the Sacred Flame as a black rift and led an all-out invasion of Natlan. It was driven back by Mavuika's Night War, then hunted into the Night Kingdom and killed there by Mavuika and the Traveler in the Version 5.3 finale of the Natlan Archon Quest. It is dead as of 7.1.

Nature: Gosoythoth had no fixed body. It was an entity of ineffable form that took shape from the Abyss's power once the Sacred Flame was gone. Unlike its monsters it could think: it worked out Mavuika's plan to awaken a last hero and moved to crush Natlan before that could happen.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. It was killed in the Night Kingdom by Mavuika and the Traveler (Where All Hopes Lie, 5.3).

31.content:
Hilichurl (also: hilichurl people, curse of the wilderness, wilderness curse, cursed Khaenri'ahns): Hilichurls are the masked, tribal creatures that attack travellers in the wilds of every nation, and most people take them for monsters. Many are in fact cursed people: Khaenri'ahns of mixed or foreign ancestry struck with the "curse of the wilderness" in the cataclysm 500 years ago. It wears away memory, speech and appearance but not life, leaving them in slow, painful decline.

Origin: After the cataclysm the gods cursed Khaenri'ahns in two ways. Pure-blood Khaenri'ahns received the curse of immortality. People whose ancestry belonged to other gods' lands received the curse of the wilderness, which turned them into monsters.

32.content:
Hilichurls (also: hilichurl tribes, Hilifolk, hill devils, hill dwellers, majuj): Hilichurls are primitive, masked humanoid monsters found in wild places all over Teyvat. They live in small tribes, speak their own language (Hilichurlian), love meat, hate vegetables, and are usually hostile to humans. Most people believe they cannot be reasoned with. Many of them are former people of Khaenri'ah who were cursed into this form during the cataclysm 500 years ago.

Nature: Hilichurls are bare-chested and barefoot, with a large mane, long ears, a loincloth, bandaged limbs, greyish-black skin and always a mask. The Archive says they resemble humans but have lost "both their intellect and spirituality".

Society: Tribes are small and scattered through the wilderness. The Samachurl (shaman) is usually the oldest member and acts like a parent: leading worship, deciding policy and defending the tribe with elemental power. Food and goods are shared according to need.

Abilities and limits: They fight with fists, clubs, rocks, crossbows and shields. Some, above all Samachurls, channel elements without a Vision; Jacob Musk calls this unexplained.

Variants: Common hilichurls (fighters, guards, shooters, grenadiers); Samachurls (elemental shamans); Mitachurls (big warriors with axes or shields); Lawachurls (mutated elemental giants: Stonehide, Frostarm, Thunderhelm); Hilichurl Rogues (tribeless Anemo or Hydro wanderers).

Relations: Hilichurls usually attack outsiders on sight, and adventurers and the Knights of Favonius fight them routinely; a few individuals will talk.

33.content:
Humans (also: mortals of Teyvat, humans of Teyvat, people of the Human Realm): Humans are the ordinary peoples of Teyvat: the ones who farm, trade, fight, worship and write. By the most complete account in the setting, the Heavenly Principles made them after conquering the dragons, and set them under a covenant with the heavens. Their fates are written in the stars, and their power over the elements comes only from a Vision, a gift tied to a strong desire. The Traveler is an outsider to this arrangement, and so are the Descenders.

Origin: The Byakuyakoku Collection preserves a banned account in which the Primordial One (whom the wiki identifies with the Heavenly Principles) fought and defeated the seven dragon sovereigns, then made humans. With one of its Shades it created animals, plants and trees, then humans, "numerous as the stars". They made a covenant with it and entered a new age, the unified civilization.

Fate and stars: The stars hold human fate. A Vision bearer's fate is tied to a constellation, a pattern of real celestial bodies called Stella Fortuna. The Heavenly Principles are said to hold humans' strings like a puppeteer. The Traveler and other Descenders are not bound, and neither are dragons, who predate Celestia's rule.

34.content:
Hydro Mimic (also: Hydro Mimics, Hydro Mimic Boar, Hydro Mimic Crane, Hydro Mimic Crab, Hydro Mimic Squirrel, Hydro Mimic Finch, Hydro Mimic Frog, Hydro Mimic Mallard): Hydro Mimics are bodies of living water shaped like ordinary animals: boars, cranes, crabs, squirrels, finches, frogs, mallards and raptor-like birds. They are pure Hydro Elemental Lifeforms, summoned in numbers by the Oceanid Rhodeia of Loch, and some are giant-sized. They are not real animals and do not behave like them.

Nature: Hydro Mimics are made entirely of Hydro and resemble normal wildlife. Like Hydro Slimes, they can walk on deep water and so cannot drown.

Abilities and limits: They fight with water: rams and charges from boars, wave-flapping and bubble attacks from cranes and crabs, a whirling vortex under mallards, leaps from frogs and finches, and diving swoops from raptors. Boars and squirrels heal themselves continually. (Gameplay-derived.)

Relations: Rhodeia of Loch, the Oceanid at Wuwang Hill in Liyue, summons them. They are otherwise only loosely tied to any person or group.

Appearances: Beyond Rhodeia, the wiki records mimics in Zhongli's Story Quest around the Guyun Stone Forest, in the Spiral Abyss during Versions 1.5 and 2.3, around Broken Isle in the Golden Apple Archipelago, and in the Chasm's underground mines.

35.content:
Hydro Tulpa (also: Awakened Egregore, Hydro Tulpa: Flashflood, Half-Tulpa): The Hydro Tulpa is a human-shaped monster formed from the agglomeration of countless drops of water. It stands as a world boss in Fontaine's Beryl Region and fights with water-formed fists, spears, hammers and swords. During the fight it keeps producing smaller Half-Tulpas and absorbs them to grow stronger. Its event panel is titled "Awakening Water".

Nature: A humanoid monster made of water. The Adventurer Handbook describes it as formed from the agglomeration of countless drops. It belongs to the Elemental Lifeform family (not the Fontemer Aberrants) and its title is "Awakened Egregore".

Abilities and limits: Water-formed fist, spear, hammer and sword attacks, a barrage of lances falling across the arena, and the ability to absorb a Half-Tulpa into itself to become stronger. Everything is Hydro.

Status as of 7.1: Still in the Beryl Region as a repeatable boss as of 7.1. I found no mention of it in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content.

36.content:
Hypostasis (also: Hypostases, Elemental Hypostasis, Elemental Hypostases): Hypostases are elemental lifeforms that have given up their old forms and structures to reach the highest level of elemental purity. Each is a compact, dense, cube-shelled core of one element, and there is a normal boss for each of the seven: Anemo, Electro, Geo, Cryo, Hydro, Pyro and Dendro. They are invulnerable while the shell surrounds them and can be hurt only when the diamond-shaped core is exposed, usually during or after an attack.

Nature: Ultra-compact, high-mass bodies of pure element. A solid shell forms around the core, and only the core responds to elemental stimuli. They are immune to their own element and deal damage of that element.

37.content:
Icewind Suite (also: Dirge of Coppelia, Nemesis of Coppelius, Gear and Clockwork Roundelay, Artificed Dancers, Coppelia and Coppelius): The Icewind Suite is a ballet-like boss fight in Fontaine: two clockwork meka dancers, Coppelia and Coppelius, built as Artificed Dancers by the Fontaine Research Institute. They wait on a garden dance floor in the Court of Fontaine Region and fight only when someone speaks to the engineer Maillardet and asks for a performance. Coppelia fights with Anemo and Coppelius with Cryo.

Nature: Clockwork meka, not living creatures: two artificed dancers shaped like a ballerina and her partner, built to perform. They belong to the Clockwork Meka group of Automatons. Their performance is described as an eternal waltz.

Abilities and limits: Skating, spinning and fan-and-cape attacks. Coppelius makes trails of ice and fires icicles from his cane; Coppelia makes pulses and orbs of wind. They can fight together or separately.

Status as of 7.1: In operation as of 7.1. I found no mention of the Icewind Suite in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content. The wiki lists Anemo and Cryo as the Suite's elements.

38.content:
Iktomisaurus (also: Iktomisaur, Iktomisaurs, Iktomisaurus Whelp, Iktomisaur chick, Cryo saurian): Iktomisaurs are the Cryo Saurians of Natlan: blue, furry, beaked, bat-like dragons of the western cliffs, living beside the Masters of the Night-Wind. They float and glide, are often seen meditating, and are the only Saurians said to have grasped the "Spiritspeaker" state. They are animals and do not speak.

Society: Iktomisaurs live on the cliffs of western Natlan, in the Tezcatepetonco Range, alongside the Masters of the Night-Wind.

39.content:
Illuminated Beast (also: Illuminated Beasts, xianshou, adeptal beast, mystical beasts of Liyue): Illuminated beasts (xianshou) are animals of Liyue that have gained supernatural power: enormous lifespans, formidable elemental combat ability and the gift of human speech. Qilin, suanni, cranes and deer are the best known. Nearly all named examples are adepti who signed a contract with Rex Lapis to protect Liyue, so the terms overlap heavily. The full-blooded ones can take human form and can have children with mortals.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 illuminated beasts are still part of Liyue life. Most live in seclusion or quietly among people. Xiao, Ganyu, Xianyun and Madame Ping appear in the world, and Chenyu Vale's suanni live in the mountains.

key: The Guide to the Dark Paradise
40.content:
Iniquitous Baptist (also: Iniquitous Baptists, Wyrdsword of Heaven's End, The Guide to the Dark Paradise, Four-Armed Envoy): The Iniquitous Baptist is a hulking, many-limbed creature of the Abyss that wields several elements at once. As a normal boss it fights with three of Cryo, Electro, Hydro and Pyro and hides behind elemental shields that rotate between those three. It speaks like a zealot, offering to cleanse the Traveler of sin and calling the Abyss a salvation. Two named individuals take this form: the Fontainian Jakob Ingold and Haden, the Abyss Order's former sword instructor.

Nature: An Abyss-family monster with additional appendages, able to bend several kinds of elemental power. The Archive adds a note left in Hangeh Afrasiyab by an unnamed scholar: the Abyss is irreconcilable with the elements, yet even gods' elements can be entrapped and distorted and made tools of abyssal will, so abyssal power looks much like an elemental item, from a Treasure Hoarder's container to a Vision.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): the boss wields three of four elements (Cryo, Electro, Hydro, Pyro), which changes daily in the overworld and is fixed in challenge modes such as the Spiral Abyss and Imaginarium Theater. It shields itself with an element and cycles through three shields. Breaking a shield paralyses it. Crystals behind it show which shield is active and which remain.

41.content: Jack Frost (also: Jack Frosts, Ledovik, Jack Frost fae, ya-ho fae): Jack Frosts are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, native to Snezhnaya. They look like short, squat snowmen with floating mitten-like hands, small orange eyes and blue cheeks, and they say little except "ya-ho". They are playful, mischievous and about as clever as cats. Lumi, the earthen-looking Jack Frost who travels with Linnea, is the one most travellers meet.

42.content:
Jadeplume Terrorshroom (also: Murkwood Fungal Raptor, The Beloved King of Fungi, Deepwood Shroomlord, Metastable Jadeplume Terrorshroom): The Jadeplume Terrorshroom is a large bird-like fungal beast, the lord of fungal beasts, living in Vissudha Field in Sumeru's rainforest. Its boss titles are The Beloved King of Fungi and Deepwood Shroomlord. It attacks with Dendro spores and its beak, and it is a normal boss.

Nature: A fungal beast shaped like a large bird with a beak and a jade-coloured tail. It lives at the heart of the woods in the company of its kin.

43.content:
Jinni (also: Jinn, Jinns, Djinn, Jinnis, desert jinn, spirits of the magic bottle): The Jinn are elemental spirits of Sumeru's deserts. They can take human or other shapes and wield great power, and they were created by the goddess Nabu Malikata. After her death they served King Deshret, typically housed in silver magic bottles, weapons or lamps. Liloupar is the best known; the Traveler meets her in Sumeru, and in 6.6 she fades away.

Nature: Jinn are elemental spirits who can assume humanoid and non-humanoid forms and hold considerable power. Legendary Jinn are drawn with human features, and the Jinni in a Sumeru folk tale is a translucent, human-like dancer with hair, eyes and clothing. They normally dwell in objects such as magic bottles or weapons rather than walking the world freely.

44.content:
Kitsune (also: fox youkai, Hakushin kitsune, Sky Kitsune, Yakan kitsune): Kitsune are fox youkai of Inazuma. They live far longer than humans, can shapeshift, and keep fox features such as ears or tails in human form. Kitsune are graded: Sky Kitsune rank highest and yakan sit two grades below. The Hakushin line was the most revered; its member the Kitsune Saiguu was worshipped as a kitsune goddess and was lost in the Cataclysm 500 years ago. As of 7.1 the best-known living kitsune is Yae Miko, Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine.

Nature: Kitsune are youkai, not animals: intelligent, long-lived and able to walk among humans. Shapeshifting is their defining talent.

Abilities and limits: Shapeshifting and long life. Yae Miko's skill calls sealed yakan spirits out of sakura branches to strike with lightning.

Society: There is no single kitsune society in the present; kitsune are few. In the past the Hakushin Clan was the most prominent kitsune family and was tied to the Grand Narukami Shrine.

Relations: The kitsune known in canon, Yae Miko and the Kitsune Saiguu, are close to the Raiden Shogun and made friends among humans. Canon pairs kitsune with the bake-danuki as tricksters and rivals (the Saiguu and Ioroi, Itaru and the tanuki merchant Dozaemon).

45.content:
Koholasaurus (also: Koholasaur, Koholasaurs, Koholasaurus Whelp, water saurian, Hydro saurian): Koholasaurs are the Hydro Saurians of Natlan, dragons of the southern springs. They are four-legged, finned and slim, and the only Saurian species that can swim. They live beside the People of the Springs. They are animals, not talkers: they act on emotion and trust in their human companions.

Society: Koholasaurs live in the springs of southern Natlan, alongside the People of the Springs.

46.content: Lantern Fae (also: legendary Lantern Fae, blue flame fae, Azure Flame): Lantern Fae are one of the rarer kinds of Snowland Fae. Their true form is a floating blue flame, which they can hide behind a human-looking shape, and they live for an indefinite time without visibly ageing. In canon the only one is Flins, who serves as a Ratnik of the Lightkeepers and keeps a lonely lighthouse in Nod-Krai.

47.content:
Statue of Marble and Brass (also: Legatus Golem, Legatus of Legion Athanatoi, Rhythm of Ruthless Flames): The "Statue of Marble and Brass", archived as the Legatus Golem, is a majestic centaur-shaped golem of marble and brass. It sleeps in the exhibition hall of the undersea Faded Castle, a relic of the sunken Remurian civilisation. Under the stone it has Ichor blood, and its shield and sword can "perform" a blazing melody of flames. Its title is "Legatus of Legion Athanatoi".

Nature: A golem in the form of a centaur, built of white stone and brass, towering like a commander of a legion. Its body is stone, but the Archive says Ichor blood flows beneath the hard exterior.

Abilities and limits: A Geo ward over its stone body, flaming sword strikes, stomps, charging slashes, shield slams that cause cascading explosions, and Pyro attacks performed as music: orbs, rings of notes and heatblades.

Status as of 7.1: Slumbering in the Faded Castle and available as a boss as of 7.1. I found no mention of it in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content.

48.content:
Leshy (also: Wildwood Leshy, Leshies, treeborn, Juvenile Tree Segment, Rugged Elder Leshy): The Leshy are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, tree-like forest spirits of Snezhnaya. They are reclusive, rarely come near towns or high roads, and prefer the wilderness and mountain forests. The wild ones, the Wildwood Leshies, fight as elite enemies, rooting themselves to heal and strengthen.

Nature: The Adventurer Handbook calls them a "reclusive breed" of Snezhnaya's fae that favours deep wilderness over towns. They grow in forests and wilds and are typically seen as stands of living wood with a visible heart.

49.content:
Maguu Kenki (also: Ingenious Machine: Marionette Swordmaster, Humanoid Automaton of Unknown Origin, Maguu Kengou, Marionette Swordmaster): The Maguu Kenki is a tall mechanical swordsman, a humanoid automaton wielding a blade and wearing a fearsome oni-style mask. It was reportedly built from the stored memory of the first master of a sword school famed for the Tengu Sweeper, went out of control and was thrown away. It cannot speak and only "talks" by crossing swords. The standard boss stands at Serpent's Head on Yashiori Island, Inazuma.

Nature: A discarded puppet-like automaton with a disciplined, human-shaped body. Puppet strings seem attached to parts of its body, matching its name. It has neither the ability nor, apparently, the will to speak.

50.content:
Melusine (also: Melusines, Mélusine): Melusines are a small, amphibious, all-female people of Fontaine, born from the remains of the dead great beast Elynas, whom they call "Father". Most live in Merusea Village, underwater inside Elynas's body in the Beryl Region; many others work in the Court of Fontaine, especially in the Marechaussee Phantom. Neuvillette is their protector and their "ideal of the perfect father".

Nature: Short, two-legged and almost faun-like, with large tails, mitten-like hands, stubby feet, sea-slug-like head "feelers" and ordinary hair. They swim well, live for centuries and do age. Each is born with a unique "token".

Abilities and limits: Small and not very dexterous, they fight poorly but investigate superbly.

key: Nameless Lord of the Great Lake
51.content:
Millennial Pearl Seahorse (also: Nameless Lord of the Great Lake, Chasm Seahorse): The Millennial Pearl Seahorse is a very large, ancient Fontemer Aberrant that dwells in a cavern in the Liffey Region of Fontaine. It is an Electro boss, and its Archive title is the Nameless Lord of the Great Lake. Legend names it one of the two sovereigns of the Fontemer Aberrants; the Archive insists the legend is romantic fancy.

Nature: The Adventurer Handbook calls it an ancient suzerain of the Fontemer Aberrants, with a body of phantasmal beauty and a temper fiercer than a raging thunderstorm. It is a seahorse-like beast with a single horn, and it carries an Electro-charged pearl. Its title reads as: the great tyrant of the Aberrants lives in a deep cavern, and few have withstood its violet, electrifying glare.

Abilities and limits: Electro attacks while its pearl is intact: it leaps and slams the ground, charges with its horn, marks a target with a circle of fish, sends homing fish-shaped missiles and swipes with its tail, leaving electrified ground behind.

52.content:
Natlan Bosses (also: Natlan normal bosses, Natlan world bosses): Natlan has seven normal bosses, arena fights in the nation of Pyro. Two are saurian beasts: Kongamato, an ancient Yumkasaurus the Scions of the Canopy revere, and Holawaqa Ngoubou, a mutated Qucusaurus. Two are ancient machines from the Secret Source ruins: the Configuration Device and the Overseer Device. The others are the Abyssal Tenebrous Papilla, the hollow Lava Dragon Statue, and the Wayward Hermetic Spiritspeaker, a reclusive priestess of the Masters of the Night-Wind.

Nature: Each boss is a distinct kind of threat: living saurians, ancient machines, an Abyssal plant, a stone-hearted lava construct and a human priestess.

Individuals: - Kongamato (Tequemecan Valley): ancient Yumkasaur king, Archived as the Gluttonous Yumkasaur Mountain King.
- Holawaqa Ngoubou (Huitztli Hill): golden-flame Qucusaur, Archived as the Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant.
- Secret Source Automaton: Configuration Device (Toyac Springs).
- Tenebrous Papilla (Quahuacan Cliff).
- Wayward Hermetic Spiritspeaker (Tezcatepetonco Range).
- Lava Dragon Statue (Atocpan).
- Secret Source Automaton: Overseer Device (Atocpan).

key: Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares
Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network
53.content:
Nod-Krai Bosses (also: Knuckle Duckle, Radiant Moonfly, Frostnight Herra, Super-Heavy Landrover: Mechanized Fortress, Super-Heavy Landrover, Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares, Lord of the Hidden Depths, Radiant Moongecko): Seven big enemies arrived with Nod-Krai between versions 6.0 and 6.7. Knuckle Duckle is a duck-shaped kuuvahki robot built by the Krumkake Craftshop's owner. The Radiant Moonfly and Radiant Moongecko are beasts steeped in ancient moonlight. Frostnight Herra is a proud moon-touched Frostnight Scion. The Super-Heavy Landrover: Mechanized Fortress is a Fatui war machine. The Lord of the Hidden Depths is an Abyssal creature watching from a rift. The Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network is an ancient machine left on the Frost Moon.

Individuals: Seven encounters, by release: Knuckle Duckle and Radiant Moonfly (6.0), Frostnight Herra (6.1), Super-Heavy Landrover (6.2), Lord of the Hidden Depths (6.3), Radiant Moongecko (6.4), Secret Source Matrix (6.7).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 all seven remain in the Nod-Krai open world as repeatable bosses.

54.content:
Oceanid (also: Oceanids, Lochfolk, Pure Water Spirit): Oceanids, also called the Lochfolk, are beings of pure Hydro born in Fontaine. They are devotees of Egeria, the first Hydro Archon, and can float, command water, and shape it into lifelike mimics. Many took human form, and the Fontainians' own ancestry is tied to that change. Some Oceanids left Fontaine long ago and now live scattered across Teyvat, such as the Spring Fairy in Mondstadt.

Nature: Oceanids are made of pure Hydro energy. They are born from the essence of water and are affected by the water they are tied to: hostility can turn their connected water bitter, while sweet water heals them.

Society: Oceanids revere Egeria, whom they regard as their master. Most no longer live in Fontaine.

Abilities and limits: Oceanids float through the air at considerable speed and manipulate water, firing Hydro attacks and creating water creatures (Hydro Mimics).

Relations: Close to Egeria in origin. Fontaine's people descend from transformed Oceanids; Focalors began as one of Egeria's Oceanid familiars before becoming Archon.

Individuals: Callirhoe, the Spring Fairy of Springvale in Mondstadt; Rhodeia of Loch on the Bishui Plain in Liyue; Idyia in the Veluriyam Mirage; Endora, who accompanies the Traveler; Ann and Mary-Ann; and Focalors, the former Hydro Archon.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no new Oceanid story was found in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content. Oceanids remain scattered across Teyvat, and Fontaine's people have been absolved as true humans.

55.content:
Oni (also: crimson oni, blue oni, Oni tribes, Oni masks): Oni are horned youkai of Inazuma, known for strength, pride, and explosive tempers. There are two tribes, the crimson oni and the blue oni. Their blood has thinned with every generation since the Cataclysm 500 years ago, so most descendants today look and act close to human. Arataki Itto, head of the Arataki Gang, is the present representative of the crimson oni.

Nature: Oni have long horns and larger builds than most humans. In ancient times they were wholly blue or wholly crimson with no markings; after generations of mixing with humans their skin became human-like, so oni now paint markings on their skin and horns to show their tribe.

Abilities and limits: Great physical strength and endurance. Itto's style is brawling and ritual combat with a heavy weapon, backed by sheer stamina.

Society: Oni historically lived secluded because humans feared them. Today oni are rare and live alongside humans, often outsiders to Inazuman society.

Relations: Oni and humans have often distrusted each other, and oni remain wary outsiders in Inazuman society.

56.content:
Pari (also: Children of Simurgh, Pari of Vourukasha Oasis): The Pari are a race of small, sentient avian beings with flower-like features who live in the Vourukasha Oasis in the Girdle of the Sands, Sumeru. They descend from the divine bird Simurgh, whose Khvarena became countless motes when mixed with the Amrita, and the sentient ones are the Pari. Each is said to have a fated responsibility, and the Traveler meets them in the 3.6 quest Khvarena of Good and Evil.

Nature: Pari look like birds with disproportionately large heads, tiny bodies and long wing-like arms, with flower-like details. They are the only form of Khvarena that is sentient. Each Pari lives to carry out one fated duty, which it must take on alone.

57.content:
Perpetual Mechanical Array (also: Perpetual Resonance SI/Ald, Bulky Iron Chunk, Big Iron Chunk): The Perpetual Mechanical Array is a strange, alien-looking war machine made of cubic parts, titled "Perpetual Resonance SI/Ald". It rests in the ruins beneath the water at Araumi, on the northern tip of Narukami Island in Inazuma. It can reshape itself into rockets, swords, blades and cubes to suit the fight.

Nature: A modular automaton of several parts rather than a single body. It is a unique Ruin machine and a boss of the Automaton family.

58.content:
Primal Construct (also: Primal Constructs, Primal Construct: Prospector, Primal Construct: Repulsor, Primal Construct: Reshaper, Architect of the Desert Palace, Primal Construct Component): Primal Constructs are the leftover machines of King Deshret's desert civilization. They are elite guardians that stand among the ruins of the Great Red Sand and inside the Mausoleum of King Deshret. The Adventurer Handbook says they guard the ruins and can punish anyone who disturbs their lord's "pure dreams." What remains of those dreams survives only in the mantras written on the machines.

Nature: These are automatons rather than animals or spirits, made for King Deshret's kingdom in Sumeru's desert. Like Ruin Machines, some stand dormant while others patrol set routes, and some simply serve as scenery among the ruins.

Abilities and limits: They fight with Physical attacks. A Primal Construct can deploy parts onto the battlefield and turn invisible, leaving the parts to attack in its place.

Location: Mainly the Great Red Sand in southern Sumeru, in its desert ruins, and the Mausoleum of King Deshret.

Relations: They are bound to the will of King Deshret, and canon names no other master.

Individuals: No individual Primal Construct has a name in canon. The Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network is the named boss variant.

59.content:
Primo Geovishap (also: Primo Geovishaps, Ancient Geovishap, Revived Primo Geovishap, Wintry Primo Geovishap): The Primo Geovishap is the largest and most ancient form of Geovishap, a dragon-like vishap of Liyue. It is met as a world boss in the cavern ruin of Tianqiu Valley, where it rises from long slumber. It is a Geo creature that always carries one extra element, shown in the colour of its scales: Pyro, Hydro, Cryo or Electro. The Adventurer Handbook calls it awesomely powerful.

Nature: A massive, scaled, lizard-like vishap of Geo, belonging to the Mystical Beasts. After many years it has grown accustomed to changes in its elemental surroundings, which is why it carries a second element drawn from the world around it.

60.content:
Prototype Cal. Breguet (also: Experimental Field Generator, Cal. Breguet, Gravity Field): Prototype Cal. Breguet is a large machine from the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, listed in the Archive as the Experimental Field Generator. It was meant to counteract gravity, but it went out of control after an accident. It now sits in the ruined Academic Assembly Hall as a Geo-attacking boss.

Nature: The Adventurer Handbook calls it a product of the Institute that has gone out of control because of an accident. The Archive describes it as an exquisite mechanical construct that once embodied an engineer's lofty ideals.

Abilities and limits: Physical attacks: sweeping laser beams from two rotating emitters, carpet bombing from the air followed by a slam, and homing missiles.

61.content:
Qucusaurus (also: Qucusaur, Qucusaurs, Qucusaurus Whelp, Qucusaur chick, flying saurian, Pyro saurian): Qucusaurs are the Pyro Saurians of Natlan: red, feathered, winged dragons of the northwestern peaks, living beside the Flower-Feather Clan. They fly, and they are proud. They are animals, not talkers, acting mostly on emotion and trust in their human companions.

Society: Qucusaurs live on the mountain peaks of northwestern Natlan and are closely tied to the Flower-Feather Clan, whose people ride them.

62.content:
Radiant Beast (also: Radiant Beasts, Radiant Antelope, Radiant Bladehorn, Radiant Lunapod, Radiant Glacial Wolf, Radiant Moonfly, Radiant Moongecko, Radiant Cocoon): Radiant Beasts are ordinary Nod-Krai animals that spent ages immersed in the power of the ancient moon and were changed by it. Infused with kuuvahki, they gained otherworldly strength, and most are attuned to a single element. They are classed as Mystical Beasts in Nod-Krai: most are elite enemies, while the Radiant Moonfly and Radiant Moongecko are world bosses.

Nature: Not a new species: an animal reshaped by moonlight over a very long time. The Adventurer Handbook says kuuvahki warped it and gave it strength beyond the natural. They use kuuvahki to fortify themselves.

63.content:
Regisvine (also: Regisvines, Cryo Regisvine, Pyro Regisvine, Electro Regisvine, Resurgent Cryo Regisvine, Sky-Searing Pyro Regisvine): Regisvines are giant plant monsters: Whopperflowers that grew huge and rooted in one place, trading their agility for a more refined store of one element. They are normal bosses, found as a Cryo Regisvine in Mondstadt, a Pyro Regisvine in Liyue and an Electro Regisvine in Sumeru. Each starts the fight inside an elemental shield at its roots or its corolla, which raises its resistances sharply until it is broken.

Nature: The Adventurer Handbook says a Whopperflower that survives many years with enough nutrition and the right environment could take root and grow into a giant tree that sways and spews elemental power. Regisvines are that stage: tall vines with a flower-like head (the corolla) and lashing tendrils, keeping to their roots instead of burrowing around as Whopperflowers do.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): a Regisvine's shield, or core, sits at its roots first. Breaking it with elemental reactions paralyses the Regisvine and strips its raised resistances. When it wakes, the core moves to the corolla, and breaking it again exposes a weak point. If the corolla core is left alone for too long, the core returns to the roots.

64.content:
Riftwolf (also: Riftwolves, Rifthound, Rifthounds, Rifthound Whelp, Wolves of the Rift, Thundercraven Rifthound, Rockfond Rifthound, Golden Wolflord): Riftwolves, also called Rifthounds or Wolves of the Rift, are pack-hunting beasts of the Abyss that travel together like wolves and are said to be able to erode the borders of the world. They were made by the alchemist Gold. They first appeared in Version 2.2, mainly on Tsurumi Island in Inazuma, and are ruled by the Golden Wolflord boss (2.3). Their attacks inflict a party-wide Corrosion that drains HP.

Nature: Dull-coloured, alien beasts with blood strong enough to dissolve the world's boundaries. They act like wolf packs, but the Abyss, not nature, is their origin.

Abilities and limits: The elites use Electro (Thundercraven) or Geo (Rockfond). Any contact, even absorbed by a shield, applies Corrosion to the whole party, draining HP over time. Smaller Whelps run with them.

65.content:
Ruin Machine (also: Ruin Machines, Ruin Guard, Ruin Guards, Ruin Hunter, Ruin Hunters, Ruin Grader, Ruin Graders, Humanoid Ruin Machines): Ruin Machines are war machines built by the lost underground nation of Khaenri'ah, whose people called the common Ruin Guard a "Field Tiller". Masterless since Khaenri'ah fell 500 years ago, they roam or lie dormant in ruins all over Teyvat, wake when people come near, and attack with fists, blades, lasers and homing missiles. "Ruin Guard" is a modern name: people mistook them for the ruins' guardians.

Nature: Automatons, not living creatures: they have no element of their own and fight mostly with physical force. A glowing eye or core is each one's weak point.

Abilities and limits: Heavy armour, crushing melee attacks, homing missiles, lasers and, for some models, flight. Hitting the exposed weak point can stun a machine for a while.

Relations: The Abyss Order scavenges them for Khaenri'ahn technology; Dainsleif, a Khaenri'ahn survivor, urges the Traveler to destroy them.

key: Giant Digging Device of the Lost Realm
66.content:
Ruin Serpent (also: Excavator: SI/Glp, Haftvad the Worm, Giant Digging Device of the Lost Realm): The Ruin Serpent is a bizarrely shaped autonomous machine that prowls the underground Chasm of Liyue, in the Serpent's Cave of The Chasm's Underground Mines. It carries a huge drilling gear on its head that can carve through bedrock. Its designation is Excavator: SI/Glp. It is one of the Ruin Machines, the automatons left by Khaenri'ah, and it is a normal boss.

Nature: A long, segmented serpent-shaped machine with a drilling gear on its head. The Handbook says it dug a tunnel to The Chasm from somewhere unknown.

67.content:
Saurian (also: Saurians, Natlan Saurians, dragons of Natlan, saurian-kind): Saurians are the dragons of Natlan. Unlike dragons elsewhere in Teyvat, they are common and live closely with humans. There are six common species, each tied to one of Natlan's six tribes: Tepetlisaurs (Geo), Yumkasaurs (Dendro), Koholasaurs (Hydro), Qucusaurs (Pyro), Iktomisaurs (Cryo) and Tatankasaurs (Electro). They are animals, not sages: most cannot speak, and they act mostly on emotion and trust in their human companions.

Society: Natlanese take Saurians as companions, and the Saurian chooses its human partner. Each species keeps a home territory that largely defines its tribe's lands, and Saurians do not cross into another species' territory uninvited.

key: Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network
68.content: Secret Source Automaton (also: Secret Source Automatons, Secret Source Automata, Secret Source machines, Secret Source Hunter-Seeker, Hunter-Seeker, Configuration Device, Secret Source Constructor, Ancient Ruins Constructor): Secret Source Automatons are machines left in Natlan by its ancient dragon civilization, and a few are also found on the Frost Moon. Most sit idle among ruins until disturbed. They bear golden inscriptions, and the fighting kinds react to a traveler's Nightsoul power. They first appeared in Version 5.0.

69.content:
Seelie (also: Seelies, Mysterious Seelie, Warming Seelie, Electro Seelie, Luminous Seelie, Seelie Court, Seelie Courts, Mini Seelie): Seelie are small, softly glowing, wisp-like creatures that drift through Teyvat's wilds, each with a pointed lower body, horn-like head parts, a flowing scarf-like trail and two trailing whiskers. A Seelie leads anyone who follows it back to its Seelie Court, a small statue, where it settles and a treasure appears. Canon explains Seelie as the devolved form of Angels, envoys of Celestia who were cursed to lose their bodies and minds. They are wordless and harmless.

Nature: Angels were envoys of Celestia, created by the Heavenly Principles and commanded to love all creatures equally. After the war of funerary flame they were cursed: any Angel who loved one individual above all others would lose body and mind. Many of the cursed now exist only as Seelie. In the Chapter V Archon Quest Beneath the Secret Source, Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night, tells the Traveler that Seelie are the devolved form of Angels.

key: The Last Prince of the Sands
70.content:
Setekh Wenut (also: The Last Prince of the Sands, Lord of the Desert, Wenut: Abnormal Turbulence): The Setekh Wenut is a giant eyeless sandworm living in the Wenut Tunnels of the Desert of Hadramaveth, in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It is a normal boss with the title The Last Prince of the Sands. It finds prey by sound and vibration and fights with Anemo blasts and by drilling out of the ground.

Nature: A huge blind predator of the deep desert, hunting through sound and vibration.

71.content:
Slime (also: Slimes, Hydro Slime, Pyro Slime, Cryo Slime, Electro Slime, Anemo Slime, Geo Slime, Dendro Slime): Slimes are pudgy elemental lifeforms found all over Teyvat, made of condensed elemental energy. They come in the seven elements and in small and large sizes, are immune to their own element, and bump, leap and slam. Canon calls them lowly creatures of minimal intelligence, but people find uses for them: hilichurls throw them, chefs cook with them, and engineers build with them.

Nature: Slimes are made of condensed elemental energy. The kind of energy fixes the element, and its concentration fixes the size. They gather in groups in places that match their element.

Abilities and limits: Slimes bump into people; large slimes also leap and slam. They shrug off their own element and carry it, so reactions with it can still happen. (Gameplay note.)

Relations: Hilichurls use slimes as weapons, balloons, and refrigerators. Chefs, engineers and tinkerers treat them as a material.

72.content:
Snegovik (also: Snegurochka, Snegurochka (female Snegovik), snow fae, Snow Maiden, Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka): The Snegovik, "snow fae", are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae. Their women are called Snegurochka. By several in-world accounts they were made for companionship and are born with incomplete souls, and only love for a human can make them whole. They live all over Snezhnaya, and their Grand Duchess traditionally resides at the House of Hesperides.

Nature: Snegovik are said to be created as servants or companions for the Hyperboreans. They are among the most numerous fae in Snezhnaya today and live across the whole nation.

key: The Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather
73.content:
Snezhnaya Bosses (also: Immortal Construct, The Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather, Chimeric Winged Lion, Solo Accompanist, Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow, Outcast Ice Shadow): Snezhnaya has three open-world bosses as of 7.1. Two are discarded creations of the alchemist Koshchei: the Immortal Construct, a feral winged beast with crimson leaf-like wings, and the Chimeric Winged Lion, a two-headed lion-and-bird chimera. The third is the Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow, an ancient Snegovik knight who has left her people's mountain manor and still trains alone in the snow.

Immortal construct: A mindless winged beast in Everfrozen Earth, titled "The Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather". It is a by-product, made only to serve someone else's plan, and now wanders the wilds with no purpose left.

Chimeric winged lion: A two-headed chimera, one head a lion and one a falcon, titled "Solo Accompanist", found in the Volkodlak Tundra. It commands Anemo and Electro power far beyond ordinary man-made monsters.

Guardian blade: An ancient Snegovik swordswoman titled "Outcast Ice Shadow", met at Fellfrost Peak in southern Snezhnaya. She left the House of Hesperides and trains alone, awaiting a day she may return.

74.content:
Snowland Fae (also: Fae, Filii Adamici Evoluti, Evolved Children of Humanity, fae of Snezhnaya): The Snowland Fae, or simply "fae", are Snezhnaya's nonhuman supernatural peoples. Hyperborean artisans created them thousands of years ago. They live alongside humans, can use elemental power without a Vision, and many can change their shape. The first Cryo Archon, the Belyi Tsar, united them, and under his rule they formed the ruling aristocracy of the Northlands. After his death in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago, the Tsaritsa took power and the fae lost most of their old privileges.

Nature: The fae vary widely. Many look nearly human, often with blue crystalline markings; others resemble animals (the Volkodlak), little snowmen (Jack Frosts) or trees (Leshy). They have their own language and script.

Abilities and limits: All fae can wield elemental energy and magic without a Vision or a Moon Wheel. Some kinds also fly, shapeshift or work ice.

75.content:
Solitary Suanni (also: Ancient Lord of the Mountains, Mist-Cloaked Paths, suanni boss): The Solitary Suanni is an illuminated beast of Chenyu Vale, Liyue, called the Ancient Lord of the Mountains. Its in-game text says it is an elegant, proud creature that lives apart from the material world in mountains shrouded in adeptal energy. As a boss it wields Anemo and Hydro against intruders on the Southern Mountain, at Chizhang Wall.

Nature: A beast of graceful form and lonesome, proud nature, in the Mystical Beasts family and attuned to Anemo and Hydro.

76.content:
Specter (also: Specters, Anemo Specter, Cryo Specter, Dendro Specter, Electro Specter, Geo Specter, Hydro Specter, Pyro Specter): Specters are small elemental lifeforms that float in the air. The Adventurer Handbook describes them as monsters born from highly concentrated elements, little sprites with a gentle temperament much like slimes, though they can sometimes explode into a rage. They exist in all seven elements and are immune to their own.

Nature: Specters are made of concentrated elemental energy and drift above the ground. They are calm by default but fly into a rage if struck hard.

Abilities and limits: They float, spit or throw elemental bolts, and have a rage state: after a very heavy hit they swell and use stronger attacks. On death they blow up. (Gameplay-derived.)

Relations: Specters have no leader or society. They share their family, the Elemental Lifeforms, with slimes.

77.content:
Tainted Hydro Phantasm (also: Tainted Hydro Phantasms, Tainted Water-Splitting Phantasm, Tainted Water-Spouting Phantasm, Hydro Phantasm, Hydro Phantasms): Tainted Hydro Phantasms are elite Hydro elemental lifeforms, strange water spirits that arose in Fontaine's waters after the Oceanids were gone. The Archive says they lack the elegance and beauty of the Oceanids, which is why they are called tainted. They come in two forms, the Water-Splitting and the Water-Spouting Phantasm.

Nature: Elemental lifeforms made of Hydro, born from Fontaine's waters. Their Archive entries call them "tainted" because they came after the calamity and lack the beauty and grace of the Oceanids.

Abilities and limits: They fire bubbles of water and, once enraged, grow larger and hit harder. They are permanently Hydro and immune to Hydro damage.

Relations: They replaced the Oceanids in Fontaine's waters; the Archive explicitly contrasts the two. Sigewinne once needed an extract from a Water-Splitting Phantasm among the ingredients for a task.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tainted Hydro Phantasms remain ordinary hostile lifeforms in Fontaine's waters. No later content found reveals their origin, and none was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya.

78.content:
Tatankasaurus (also: Tatankasaur, Tatankasaurs, Tatankasaurus Whelp, charging saurian, Electro saurian): Tatankasaurs are the Electro Saurians of Natlan: huge, horned, buffalo-like dragons of the volcanic southwest, living beside the Collective of Plenty. They are usually docile, but an angered Tatankasaur cannot be reasoned with until its energy runs out. They are animals and do not speak.

Society: Tatankasaurs live in the volcanic regions of Natlan's southwest, around Atocpan, with the Collective of Plenty.

79.content:
Tenebrous Mimiflora (also: Tenebrous Mimifloras, Tenebrous Mimesis, Tenebrous Papilla, Void Obliterator Bubble, Void Fantasy Plant): Tenebrous Mimifloras are plant-like monsters of the Abyss found in Natlan. They enter battle disguised as other creatures, protected by a Void Ward, and fall back to their true form when the ward breaks. Their largest form is the Tenebrous Papilla, a boss at Quahuacan Cliff that mimics other bosses. Their attacks inflict Attrition, a slow loss of health.

Nature: Archive text calls them Abyssal monsters that descended from a twisted, alien world. Where the corrosive waves of the dark tide lap, such plant-like monsters are said to grow.

Abilities and limits: Mimicry: on entering battle it may take the shape of another enemy, and in that form it cannot be damaged until its Void Ward is destroyed. Its true form fires spikes and homing spheres.

80.content:
Tengu (also: crow tengu, Great Tengu, Yougou Tengu, tengu warrior): Tengu are youkai of Inazuma with black wings and crow-faced masks. They are swift, skilled with the bow and sword, and strong beyond their slim frames. Most lived in seclusion; the elite Yougou Tengu guarded Mt. Yougou and the Grand Narukami Shrine. The tengu most people meet today is Kujou Sara, a general of the Tenryou Commission who was adopted into the Kujou Clan and serves the Raiden Shogun with unbroken devotion.

Nature: Black wings are a common trait (Teruyo, Sara), and every known tengu wears a crow mask. Sara has two pairs of raven-black wings and a red crow mask at the side of her head.

Abilities and limits: Flight, archery, swordsmanship and speed. Tengu arts are taught beyond their own clans.

Society: Tengu live mostly in seclusion in forests and mountains. The Yougou Tengu are an elite group who protected Mt. Yougou, and so the Grand Narukami Shrine on it.

Relations: Tengu have served or allied with the Raiden Shogun and the Narukami kitsune. They appear alongside the oni in Inazuman tales and duels.

81.content:
Tepetlisaurus (also: Tepetlisaur, Tepetlisaurs, Tepetlisaurus Whelp, Tepetlisauri): Tepetlisaurs are the Geo Saurians of Natlan: bipedal, lizard-like dragons with large brown bodies, rocky protrusions and a drill-shaped horn on the forehead. They live in the mines of eastern Natlan alongside the Children of Echoes, and can tunnel through rock and even solid Phlogiston.

Nature: Tepetlisaurs are strong-clawed, rock-armoured animals. Their drill-horn and claws let them dig through stone and solid Phlogiston, and they climb crystals of solid Phlogiston easily.

Society: Tepetlisaurs belong to the Children of Echoes and live in the mines of eastern Natlan. Like other Saurians they choose their human partners and keep to their own tribe's territory.

Abilities and limits: Tepetlisaurs fight with their drill-horn and claws, striking with Geo force. They burrow into the ground and travel under it, then burst out to slam down on a target.

Relations: Their human partners are the Children of Echoes. Among the other species they are the miners' counterpart to the forest Yumkasaurs of the Scions of the Canopy.

Individuals: Little One, a Tepetlisaur whelp marked by the Flamelord's Blessing and called the "Chosen of Dragons" by Kukulkan, accompanies the Traveler in the Natlan world story. The young Tepetlisaur Aguara appears in Linnea's Story Quest.

82.content:
