Thunder Manifestation (also: Raging Thunder of Amakumo Peak, Crackling Thunder Manifestation, Stormy Resentment): The Thunder Manifestation is an unusual Electro lifeform, a giant violet bird of lightning that haunts Amakumo Peak on Seirai Island in Inazuma. It looks somewhat like an Oceanid but lacks her intelligence or memories. What drives it is raw, primal fury that the texts variously call resentment, hatred or regret.

Nature: An Electro elemental lifeform of lightning and storm. It does not speak or reason like an Oceanid, and acts from a single overwhelming emotion.

83.content:
Tighnarian (also: Tighnarians, Valuka Shuna, Tighnarian people): The Tighnarians, called Valuka Shuna ("large desert dog") by the Aranara, are a humanoid, foxlike people of Sumeru. They came from Tighnar and served King Deshret in the Great Red Sand. After his fall they lived in Tulaytullah and later moved to the rainforest. Tighnari, the Forest Watcher, is one of their descendants.

Nature: Hermanubis, the only "true" Tighnarian shown, had a jackal-like head and a humanlike body. Mortal descendants such as Tighnari are mostly human, with big fennec-like ears and bushy tails.

84.content:
Tri-Lakshana Creature (also: Tri-Lakshana Creatures, Tri-Lakshana, Trilakshana creature, Tri-Yana Seed, Seed Mirror, Bouncy Mushroom, Rocklifting Branch): Tri-Lakshana Creatures are special plants and fungi of Sumeru that change when elemental energy touches them. Normally they sit in a Normal state; Pyro leaves them Scorched, and Electro makes them Activated. The Sumeru tutorial tells travellers to use their different forms to aid an adventure.

Nature: The in-game tutorial calls them creatures that can transform due to stimuli from external elemental energy. Contact with Electro puts them in an Activated state; contact with Pyro puts them in a Scorched state. Their Normal state is associated with Dendro.

85.content:
Umibouzu (also: Umibozu): Umibouzu are huge, intelligent sea creatures known in Inazuma, extinct in most waters. Sailors regard them as foes and many were hunted; the people of Watatsumi Island instead treat each as a lonely individual. They appear only through the world quest Solitary Sea-Beast (2.1).

Nature: Huge, intelligent, docile and solitary sea animals.

Society: Mostly solitary. Watatsumi's people give each creature its own name rather than a species name.

86.content:
Ursa the Drake (also: Ursa, Ursa's Flesh, the drake Ursa): Ursa the Drake was an Angel that gave up wisdom for raw power and became a corrupted dragon, said to have no distinct element. A thousand years ago it hounded Vennessa's tribe and menaced Mondstadt until Barbatos helped drive it off, after which it was sealed. Four years before the game's story the Fatui and the Knights' inspector Eroch unsealed it for experiments, and its flesh was still being exploited in Mondstadt in the Lohen story quest.

Nature: A draconic devolved Angel. Wiki summaries describe it as having abandoned wisdom for power, and it is not tied to a particular element. It controlled hilichurls, and could speak or at least understand speech.

87.content:
Vila (also: Vilas, wind fae, Grand Duke of the Vila, Grand Duchess of the Vila): The Vila are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae. They are small, pale fae with pointed, green-tipped ears and two pairs of insect-like wings that allow brief flight. They were among the first to follow the Belyi Tsar, supplied most of the Druzhna guard, and the playable Vesna, Commander of the Druzhna, is one.

Nature: Vila are humanoid and small in stature, with pale white skin, pointed ears tipped in green and some with a green triangle under the eyes. They fly briefly on insect-like wings, which gives them exceptional mobility.

88.content:
Vishap (also: Vishaps, Dragonheirs, elemental vishaps): Vishaps are dragon-like elemental creatures of the Light Realm. They once followed each of the Seven Sovereigns by element and were the dominant race of the world; over long ages they are said to evolve into true dragons. Three lines are known today: the Geovishaps of Liyue, the Bathysmal Vishaps of Enkanomiya (with newcomers in Fontaine) and the Pyro vishaps of Natlan, who lost their intelligence and became Saurians.

Nature: Vishaps are elemental creatures of the Light Realm, also called the Vishap Realm or Elemental Realm. They are reptilian, dragon-like beasts rather than people, and where players meet them they are hostile to humans.

Geovishaps: Geovishaps live in Liyue's mountains and have done so since a bygone era, together with their lord Azhdaha. They attune to Geo; adults can also take on Cryo, Electro, Pyro or Hydro one at a time during a fight, drawing on nearby elemental energy.

Bathysmal vishaps: Bathysmal Vishaps, also called the Dragonheirs of the Depths or Hydro Vishaps, once ruled Enkanomiya and the depths below it. Their attacks can drain Energy. They hate artificial light.

Relations: Vishaps follow the Dragon Sovereigns, whom Bathysmal Vishaps see as the peak of their kind. Liyue's Geovishaps follow Azhdaha. Humans meet them as threats, though Liyue has lived beside them for ages.

89.content:
Volkodlak (also: Volkodlaks, Volkodlak Brute, Volkodlak Brutes, beast fae, Miscislavli): The Volkodlak are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, the non-human spirits of Snezhnaya. They are beast-like but humanoid, strong and keen-sensed, and the Adventure Handbook calls them the most populous fae race in the nation. About 3,000 years ago their kings led the Miscislavli Alliance, which the first Cryo Archon, the Belyi Tsar, broke in war. Today they appear as a nation's worth of clans, a few mild or loyal, and as the Volkodlak Brutes that attack travellers in the Snezhnayan wilds.

Nature: Like other fae, Volkodlak were made by the artisans of Hyperborea, the "Golden City", as part of an effort to build a race that could surpass humans. They stand and work on two legs with beast features and the strength of animals. They are long-lived, though lifespans differ across fae kinds.

Society: Historically the Volkodlak were ruled by a king. Their great confederation was the Miscislavli Alliance. Since the Belyi Tsar absorbed the fae kingdoms into the Pale Star Court, they have no king of their own, and clans have different loyalties and roles.

History: About 3,000 years ago King Miscislav, the "Blood-Devourer", ruled the Miscislavli Alliance as a rival of the first Emperor, Monomakh Snezhnyi. After a short war the Emperor killed Miscislav in battle and became the Belyi Tsar.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Volkodlak are an ordinary part of Snezhnayan life and wildlife-like threats, with no ruler. Their Tundra of Ancient Beasts is a region of the Snezhnayan map.

90.content: Water Imp (also: Water Imps, Rusalka, Siren, Sirens, Vodyanitsa kin): Water Imps are a less common kind of Snowland Fae from Snezhnaya, also called Rusalka or Sirens. They have fin-shaped ears, a fish tail in water that becomes two legs on land, very sharp hearing and a gift for song. Most left Snezhnograd long ago; Vodyanitsa, the prima donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe, stayed.

91.content:
Wayob (also: Great Spirits, ancestral wills of Natlan): The Wayob are the great spirits venerated by Natlan's six tribes, believed to embody the will of each tribe's ancestors. They have no body and live in the Night Kingdom, from which they guard their people against the Abyss. Each tribe calls on its own Wayob for protection and blessing. The Abyss's invasion of the Night Kingdom infected them, but they recovered once it was cleansed.

Nature: According to the Dreamseeker Priest, a Wayob is "will without form or thought". Wayob are not physically present in Natlan, but can manifest there through obsidian totems and Nightsouls. They can see the past and future.

92.content:
Wayob Manifestation (also: Wayob Manifestations, Flow-Inverted Wayob Manifestation, Foliar-Swift Wayob Manifestation, Rock-Cavernous Wayob Manifestation, Biting-Cold Wayob Manifestation, Burning-Aflame Wayob Manifestation, Thundering Wayob Manifestation): Wayob Manifestations are elite enemies in Natlan, the form in which the Wayob revered by the six tribes show themselves on the land. They look like obsidian totems or statues and appear through totems and Nightsouls. There are six types, one for each tribe and element: Flow-Inverted (Hydro), Foliar-Swift (Dendro), Rock-Cavernous (Geo), Biting-Cold (Cryo), Burning-Aflame (Pyro) and Thundering (Electro).

Nature: Archive text says the Wayob is a belief that grew from the tribes and obsidian totems once Natlan began to communicate with the realm of the Lord of the Night. A Wayob is a consciousness of collective thought and the home of the ancestors' souls.

Abilities and limits: Gameplay (not literal lore): a Manifestation periodically raises a ward and a field around itself. The ward blocks all damage, and the field drains Energy from the whole party while the active character stands in it.

93.content:
Whopperflower (also: Whopperflowers, Cryo Whopperflower, Pyro Whopperflower, Electro Whopperflower, Vanagni, mimetic plant monster): Whopperflowers are elemental plant monsters found all over Teyvat. They hide as Sweet Flowers, Mint or Small Lamp Grass and burst out when someone tries to pick them, then fight with Cryo, Pyro or Electro. They have high resistance to every damage type, and given enough time and food they grow into huge Regisvines.

Nature: Mimetic plants that lurk beneath the surface and ambush unsuspecting prey, taking years, plentiful nutrition and the right environment to put down roots and become a giant tree that sways and spews elemental power.

Abilities and limits: They attack with their element, burrow underground to reposition, and periodically raise an elemental shield while charging up a special attack. Breaking the shield in time paralyses them and lowers their resistance.

94.content:
The Wild Hunt (also: Wild Hunt, Wasteland Wild Hunt, Wilderness Ghoul, Wilderness Ghouls, Wilderness Hunter, Wilderness Exile): The Wild Hunt is an Abyssal phenomenon, and the horde of monsters it produces, in Nod-Krai. It taints the dead with Abyssal energy and turns them into ghouls that wander the frozen wilderness, usually when dark mist rolls in. Its source is Rerir, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, whose body was torn into fragments scattered across the land. It attacked Nod-Krai for years looking for the pieces of him and the power of the moons.

Nature: Not a species and not a single creature. It is a distributed Abyssal phenomenon: wherever a fragment of Rerir lies, monsters gather. The ghouls themselves are described on the wiki as former humans cursed by the Abyss and doomed to wander the frozen wastes.

95.content:
Wildlife (also: Teyvat wildlife, Teyvat fauna, wild animals of Teyvat): Wildlife are the ordinary animals of Teyvat: birds, beasts, fish, and small creatures such as frogs, crabs and fireflies. Most are harmless and flee when approached. Each region has its own species, and a few carry folk legends.

Nature: Wildlife are natural animals, not elemental creatures. Most are skittish; a few are dangerous.

96.content:
Youkai (also: yokai): Youkai are Inazuma's supernatural beings. They outlive humans, have their own natures, and once powerful enough can take human form. Kinds include kitsune, tengu, oni, bake-danuki (tanuki), nekomata, yumekui-baku, kappa and tsukumogami. Many died fighting the Abyss in the Cataclysm 500 years ago; today they are few and their bloodlines thin. Known present-day youkai include Yae Miko (kitsune), Yumemizuki Mizuki (baku), Kirara (nekomata), Kujou Sara (tengu) and Arataki Itto (part oni).

Nature: Many youkai have a true form and a human one; tails, horns or wings often show even in human shape. Inazumans believe everything has a spirit and honour local spirits at small shrines.

Abilities and limits: Shape-shifting, long life, and powers by kind: kitsune and tanuki trickery, tengu flight and martial skill, oni strength, baku eating nightmares.

97.content:
Yumekui-Baku (also: Yumekui Baku, baku, dream eaters, dream-eating youkai): Yumekui-baku, or baku, are lesser youkai of Inazuma who enter, shape and eat dreams. In their original form they are small, round and squishy with curly tails. Only some can take human form. Yumemizuki Mizuki is the best-known baku and works as a clinical psychologist at Aisa Bathhouse.

Nature: Small floating dream-eaters, gentle and mostly unable to fight.

Abilities and limits: Enter and influence the dreams of humans and other youkai, eat them, and rarely fight.

Society: Quiet, helpful folk with no known central leadership; rarely seen in groups.

Relations: Gentle toward humans and other youkai, who rely on them for relief from nightmares.

Yumkasaurus (also: Yumkasaur, Yumkasaurs, Yumkasaurus Whelp, Yumkasauri): Yumkasaurs are the Dendro Saurians of Natlan: bipedal, lizard- or chameleon-like dragons with slim green bodies, feathery ears, large cheeks and a round, fluffy tail. They live in the forests of southeastern Natlan alongside the Scions of the Canopy.

Nature: Yumkasaurs have strong hind legs and a fluffy tail. They use their tongues as grappling hooks to swing through the air and scale walls, and keep Flamegranate pectin in their cheek pouches to spit at distant objects and wrap around them.

Society: Yumkasaurs belong to the Scions of the Canopy and live in the trees of the south-east. Like other Saurians they choose their human partners and stay in their own tribe's territory.

Abilities and limits: Yumkasaurs fight with their claws, tail and tongue, using Dendro power. They grapple with the tongue to swing forward and can climb cliffs, though less efficiently than Tepetlisaurs.

Relations: Their human partners are the Scions of the Canopy. They are the forest counterpart of the mining Tepetlisaurs of the Children of Echoes.

Individuals: Kongamato, the ancient "Mountain King", is a Yumkasaur revered by the Scions of the Canopy. He fought beside the hero Burkina during the Cataclysm.

99.content:
Zombie (also: Jiangshi, the undead, Liyue zombie): In Liyue a zombie is a dead person brought back into suspended animation, by adeptal energy or by medicine. The body stays cold and stiff, and talismans help sustain the state. Two are known: Qiqi, the herb-gathering apprentice of Bubu Pharmacy, and Jialiang, a husband and father revived by Baizhu's Elixir of Immortality.

Nature: A zombie can look like an ordinary person at a glance, but the body is cold and stiff, as in rigor mortis, so zombies are usually forced to move by hopping. Talismans on the body help sustain suspended animation. Zombies need orders before they act.

Individuals: Qiqi and Jialiang.
